<STRUCT_0001>
Any smooth local property of germs of schemes gives rise to a corresponding
property of algebraic stacks. Note that a property of germs which is smooth
local is also <ACCENT_0001>tale local. Hence for a smooth local property of germs of
schemes <MATH_0001> we know what it means to say that an algebraic space <MATH_0002> has
property <MATH_0003> at <MATH_0004>, see
Properties of Spaces, Section <REF_0001>.

Let <MATH_0001> be an algebraic stack.
Let <MATH_0002> be a point of <MATH_0003>.
Let <MATH_0004> be a property of germs of schemes which is smooth local, see
Descent, Definition <REF_0001>.
The following are equivalent
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> for any smooth morphism <MATH_0005> with <MATH_0006> a scheme
and <MATH_0007> with <MATH_0008> we have <MATH_0009>,
<STRUCT_0003> for some smooth morphism <MATH_0010> with <MATH_0011> a scheme
and some <MATH_0012> with <MATH_0013> we have <MATH_0014>,
<STRUCT_0004> for any smooth morphism <MATH_0015> with <MATH_0016> an algebraic space
and <MATH_0017> with <MATH_0018> the algebraic space <MATH_0019> has property
<MATH_0020> at <MATH_0021>, and
<STRUCT_0005> for some smooth morphism <MATH_0022> with <MATH_0023> an
algebraic space and some <MATH_0024> with <MATH_0025> the algebraic space
<MATH_0026> has property <MATH_0027> at <MATH_0028>.
<STRUCT_0006>
If <MATH_0029> is representable, then this is equivalent to
<MATH_0030>. If <MATH_0031> is an algebraic space then
this is equivalent to <MATH_0032> having property <MATH_0033> at <MATH_0034>.
